old: just as I also received authority from my Father. And I will give him the morning star.
new: just as I also received from my Father. And I will give him the morning star.
reason: Latin “accepi a Patre meo” has no object; the English added “authority”, which the Latin lacks.

old: But because you are lukewarm, neither cold nor hot, I am about to vomit you out of my mouth.
new: But because you are lukewarm, neither cold nor hot, I will begin to vomit you out of my mouth.
reason: Latin “incipiam te evomere” means “I will begin to vomit”; the English “I am about to” rendered the Greek instead.

old: Around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and on the thrones sat twenty-four elders, clothed in white garments, with golden crowns upon their heads.
new: Around the throne were twenty-four seats, and on the thrones sat twenty-four elders, clothed in white garments, with golden crowns upon their heads.
reason: Latin “sedilia” means seats; the English “thrones” rendered the Greek word instead.

old: From the throne came flashes of lightning, voices, and thunder. Seven lamps of fire burned before the throne; these are the seven spirits of God.
new: From the throne came flashes of lightning, voices, and thunder. Seven lamps burned before the throne; these are the seven spirits of God.
reason: Latin “septem lampades ardentes” has no “of fire”; the English added it from the Greek.

old: Another horse went out, fiery red. Its rider was given power to take peace from the earth, so that people would kill one another, and a great sword was given to him.
new: Another horse went out, red. Its rider was given power to take peace from the earth, so that people would kill one another, and a great sword was given to him.
reason: Latin “rufus” means red; “fiery red” follows the Greek rather than this Latin.

old: because the Lamb in the midst of the throne will shepherd them and lead them to springs of the water of life, and God will wipe every tear from their eyes.”
new: because the Lamb in the midst of the throne will rule them and lead them to springs of the water of life, and God will wipe every tear from their eyes.”
reason: Latin “reget” means “will rule”; “will shepherd” renders the Greek rather than this Latin.

old: and swore by him who lives through ages of ages, who created heaven and what is in it, the earth and what is in it, and the sea and what is in it, that there would be no further delay,
new: and swore by him who lives through ages of ages, who created heaven and what is in it, the earth and what is in it, and the sea and what is in it, that time would be no more,
reason: Latin "tempus non erit amplius" means "time will be no more"; "no further delay" rendered the Greek-English interpretation instead of the Latin.

old: I will grant authority to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy for a thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.”
new: I will give to my two witnesses, and they will prophesy for a thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth.”
reason: Latin "dabo duobus testibus meis" has no object; "authority" was supplied from the Greek-English and is not in the Latin.

old: I saw another angel flying through midheaven, holding an eternal gospel to proclaim to those who dwell upon the earth and to every nation, tribe, tongue, and people.
new: I saw another angel flying through midheaven, holding an eternal gospel to proclaim to those who sit upon the earth and to every nation, tribe, tongue, and people.
reason: Latin "sedentibus super terram" means those sitting upon the earth; "who dwell" gave the KJV's dwelling reading instead of this Latin.

old: The angel put forth his sharp sickle upon the earth, gathered the earth’s vine, and cast the grapes into the great winepress of God’s wrath.
new: The angel put forth his sharp sickle upon the earth, gathered the earth’s vine, and cast it into the great winepress of God’s wrath.
reason: Latin "misit in lacum" has no stated object; the English added "the grapes", now "it".

old: It was granted to her to clothe herself in fine linen, bright and clean. For the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints.
new: It was granted to her to clothe herself in fine linen, bright and white. For the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints.
reason: Latin “candido” means “white”, not “clean”; the English had taken the Greek-based sense instead of the Latin.
